query: Does bilateral chemogenetic inactivation of OB-projecting cholinergic neurons impair learning of the olfactory discrimination task, and is this impairment reversible upon cessation of CNO?

analyse_plan.Objective: Assess the behavioral impact of bilateral cholinergic inactivation on olfactory task learning by tracking success rates over training days in hM4D(Gi) vs. mCherry groups during the CNO-training period, and assess reversibility by tracking hM4D(Gi) animals after CNO cessation.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify bilateral targeting of OB-projecting cholinergic neurons; confirm that CNO was administered before each training session during the CNO-training block; confirm that the recovery period begins after the final CNO session; verify inclusion of the hM4D(Gi) no-CNO recovery group; verify that the visual mapping between the two sigstars and the two Two-way ANOVA effects is consistent with the statistical semantics (horizontal bar spanning the time axis = day effect; vertical bar connecting the two group curves at a single time point = group effect).
analyse_plan.Steps:
1. Bilaterally inject retrograde AAV-Cre-dependent Flp into OB and Flp-dependent hM4D(Gi)-mCherry (experimental, n = 5) or mCherry (control, n = 5) into BF of ChAT-Cre mice.
2. Train animals every two days, with CNO administered intraperitoneally at 5 mg/kg, 30 minutes prior to each training session, for 9 sessions covering days 1-17.
3. After the 9 CNO sessions, continue training the hM4D(Gi) animals without CNO over days 19-21 to assess recovery.
4. For each animal and each training day, compute the behavioral success rate (fraction of correct trials).
5. Plot success rate vs. training day as mean ± SEM for three groups: hM4D(Gi)+CNO (blue, days 1-17), mCherry+CNO (pink, days 1-17), and hM4D(Gi) no-CNO recovery (magenta, days 19-21).
6. Perform a Two-way ANOVA on the days 1-17 CNO training period with two factors: group (hM4D(Gi) vs. mCherry) and day. This yields two main effect p values: a group effect and a day effect.
7. Annotate the plot with two significance markers corresponding to the two ANOVA main effects: the horizontal sigstar (***) on top of the plot, spanning days 1-17, corresponds to the day effect (significant change in success rate across training days); the vertical sigstar (***) positioned at day 17 (the last CNO training day), connecting the mCherry curve (~0.75) and the hM4D(Gi)+CNO curve (~0.55), corresponds to the group effect (significant difference between hM4D(Gi) and mCherry groups).
8. Save success rate data and Two-way ANOVA results.

statistical_info.number: 2.26e-7 (Two-way ANOVA, day factor; horizontal sigstar spanning days 1-17)
4.71e-6 (Two-way ANOVA, hM4D(Gi) vs. mCherry; vertical sigstar at day 17)

key_analysis_results: Over the 9 CNO training sessions covering days 1-17, bilateral inactivation of OB-projecting cholinergic neurons (hM4D(Gi)+CNO group, blue) led to significantly impaired learning compared to mCherry+CNO controls (pink). A Two-way ANOVA on the days 1-17 CNO training period with factors group (hM4D(Gi) vs. mCherry) and day yielded a significant group effect (P = 4.71 × 10⁻⁶) and a significant day effect (P = 2.26 × 10⁻⁷). The horizontal sigstar on top of the plot, spanning days 1-17, corresponds to the day effect (significant change in success rate across training days, reflecting that both groups showed learning over time). The vertical sigstar positioned at day 17 (the last CNO training day), connecting the mCherry curve (success rate ~0.75) and the hM4D(Gi)+CNO curve (success rate ~0.55), corresponds to the group effect (significant difference between hM4D(Gi) and mCherry groups). After cessation of CNO, hM4D(Gi)-expressing mice (magenta, hM4D(Gi) no-CNO group) reached expertise within three additional training sessions (days 19-21), with their success rate rising from approximately 0.55 (last CNO day) to approximately 0.75 (day 21). n = 5 mice per group. Data presented as mean ± SEM.
key_analysis_conclusions: OB-projecting cholinergic neurons are behaviorally necessary for normal olfactory discrimination learning. The impairment is acute (reversible upon CNO cessation), demonstrating that cholinergic feedback actively contributes to olfactory task performance rather than merely facilitating synaptic plasticity for permanent memory formation.

summary_report.abstract: Bilateral chemogenetic inactivation of OB-projecting cholinergic neurons significantly impairs olfactory discrimination learning, with rapid recovery upon cessation of inactivation.
summary_report.methods: ChAT-Cre mice received bilateral injections of retrograde AAV-Cre-dependent Flp into OB and Flp-dependent hM4D(Gi)-mCherry (experimental, n = 5) or mCherry (control, n = 5) into BF. Animals were trained every two days, with CNO (5 mg/kg, intraperitoneal, 30 min prior to training) administered for 9 sessions covering days 1-17. After the CNO training period, hM4D(Gi) animals continued training without CNO over days 19-21 to assess recovery. Success rate (fraction of correct trials) was plotted as mean ± SEM per training day. A Two-way ANOVA on the days 1-17 CNO training period with factors group (hM4D(Gi) vs. mCherry) and day was performed.
summary_report.results: Two-way ANOVA day effect (significant change in success rate across training days, days 1-17): P = 2.26 × 10⁻⁷ (horizontal sigstar on top of the plot spanning days 1-17). Two-way ANOVA group effect (hM4D(Gi) vs. mCherry, days 1-17): P = 4.71 × 10⁻⁶ (vertical sigstar at day 17, connecting the mCherry and hM4D(Gi)+CNO curves). After CNO cessation, hM4D(Gi) animals reached expertise within 3 additional training sessions (days 19-21), with success rate rising from ~0.55 to ~0.75.
summary_report.discussion: The behavioral impairment causally demonstrates the importance of OB-projecting cholinergic neurons for olfactory discrimination. The rapid recovery indicates that the deficit is due to acute loss of cholinergic modulation during task performance rather than impaired plasticity.
